articles.title: Squeezy olive oil bottles, Meghan’s pot filler tap and the rise of ‘cheffy’ kit in home kitchens
articles.summary: Social media ‘chefluencers’ and open restaurant kitchens have made chefs more visible and inspired aspirational gadget-buying. The Duchess of Sussex is no ordinary home cook, but when Meghan appeared on Instagram this week at a hob presided over by a special pot filler tap, it spoke to a shift in…
body: While the pot filler is now most often found in luxury residential kitchens, it was reportedly invented in the early 20th century as a functional fixture for commercial kitchens. It joins a wealth of other restaurant equipment to have infiltrated our homes, from squeezy olive oil bottles to stainless steel mixing bowl sets.
At Sous Chef, a UK-based independent speciality food brand, sales of chef presses are up 26%, while sales of chef’s trays are booming, according to Holly Thomson, the company’s food editor.

For Ella Risbridger, author of The Kitchen Book: Good Food for Every Day: “It’s an amazing thing, the blurring of lines between restaurant and home kitchens.” A byproduct of the increasing visibility we have of professional chefs at work, whether via open kitchens in restaurants or “chefluencers” on social media, the utilitarianism and gadgets of restaurant kitchens are increasingly aspirational. This week, in a home tour with Architectural Digest, Julianne Moore showed off her Ikea industrial shelves.

articles.title: ‘There is no secret agenda’: Nara Smith on home-making absolutely everything, raising four kids at 25 – and why she’s definitely not a tradwife
articles.summary: The model, actor and influencer is known for making her own frozen yoghurt, bubblegum or even toothpaste while dressed in immaculate haute couture. But she insists she is not who the internet thinks she is. Nara Smith is not a tradwife, she wants you to know that.
body: Smith wants you to scrap everything you think you know about her and start again. She also doesn’t care if you don’t. As with her content: “Those that get it, get it. Those that don’t, don’t. And that’s totally fine. I tell people: ‘If you don’t like my content, I won’t see you scroll past me.’ ‘If you need to block me for your own sanity, please do. I promise I won’t know.’ And if you want to stick around, that is beautiful, I’m grateful, welcome.”

These clips blow people’s minds. Her grilled cheese video has been viewed 49.6m times. Elsewhere she’s made Nutella, ketchup, Cheez-Its, Pop-Tarts, Skittles and Snickers. She’s even made bubblegum. There’s the novelty of the recipes – she now has a cookbook of scratch-made ones, Homemade, coming out. Then there’s the outfits. She wore a $5,000 cashmere Prada suit to make chicken drumsticks, a $10,000 Schiaparelli to grate tomatoes for a gnocchi sauce. Nigella, Gwyneth, your domestic goddessing has been out-luxed.

articles.title: ‘Our town is making jeans again’: meet the firm reviving jobs and skills in Wales
articles.summary: In the first article in a series on high end British manufacturing, we visit the Hiut Denim factory in Cardigan. Worn on the streets of London’s Soho, San Francisco or Sydney, every pair of high-end jeans made by Hiut Denim comes from the rather unlikely location of a small coastal town in west…
body: Cardigan, with a population of just 4,200, has a proud history of denim production and was once home to Britain’s largest jeans factory, even if the town’s name recalls a different garment entirely.
When jeans manufacturing in Wales was moved abroad at the start of the century, hundreds of local people lost their jobs and were forced to find work elsewhere.

Hiut Denim was founded by David and Clare Hieatt in Cardigan in 2011. The couple, both originally from Wales, previously ran the ethical fashion brand Howies. They set up Hiut – the brand name blends their surname with the word utility – with the goal of reviving denim-making skills in the town and training up the next generation of skilled craftspeople.

Elin Evans was one of those “grand masters”, as they are known in the company, with a lifetime’s experience of making jeans. Now 59, Evans is Hiut’s factory manager and has been in the trade since 1983, when she was 16.

articles.title: ‘They looked like two curtain-twitchers, though not very subtle ones’: Peter Crome’s best phone picture
articles.summary: The photographer was walking home in London when he caught the attention of a pair of canine snoops. Walking home after dropping his little girl at school, Peter Crome sensed he was being watched.
body: The cause of his disquiet that day was, to his happy surprise, these two dogs. “It was such a comical moment,” he says. “They looked like two curtain-twitchers, though not very subtle ones. I liked how they were perfectly framed with the different layers of window frames, and the brickwork and hedge provided some pleasing textures, but it was the disapproving expression on their faces that made the photo for me.”

Crome waited for a while as the dogs watched other passersby, turning their heads in unison. He crossed the road to draw their attention, then took a single photo on his iPhone 14 Pro. “This is the sort of picture I would have sent my mum before she passed away a couple of years ago. I think this one would have really tickled her,” Crome says.

articles.title: On Her Triumphant New Album, Remi Wolf Gets Down in the Mud
articles.summary: After a grueling tour, a breakup, and reembracing sobriety, the singer-songwriter decamped to Big Bear and Joshua Tree to craft “Mud,” her most mature, liberating record to date.
body: If Remi Wolf’s earlier records were kaleidoscopes of maximalist, funk-inflected indie pop and surrealist lyrics, Mud marks a shift to something more mature and earthy—quite literally, with the album cover presenting the California-born singer-songwriter beaming through a sludgy mask of literal mud.

After a year that saw Wolf release her terrific sophomore album, Big Ideas; boost her own tour with an opening slot for Olivia Rodrigo; but also suffer a major breakup and become totally burned out, the seeds of the new record were planted during a two-week retreat in Nashville in late 2024, where Wolf set out to blow open her creative world by writing with total strangers. But while Nashville yielded some sparks—including the euphoric, country-tinged standout track “Champagne”—it also made her realize that what she really needed was to create her own sanctuary.

articles.title: How to Plan a Spa-Hopping Trip Across Vancouver Island
articles.summary: From floating bathhouses to geothermal hot springs in ancient rainforests, Adrienne Matei journeys across Vancouver Island and finds that wellness is woven into the landscape of British Columbia's wild Pacific coast.
body: I'm sitting neck deep in a hot tub, watching a float plane land. Moments earlier, I was in a cold plunge pool and soon I’ll be scooping handfuls of magnesium-infused salt from a glittering pile and scrubbing the mainland off my skin. I’m at HAVN, a floating sauna experience built on a refurbished naval barge moored in the harbor of Victoria, the biggest city on Vancouver Island in British Columbia —and the first stop on a trip around Vancouver Island that I’m referring to as a spa safari, thanks to the abundance of nature-infused wellness offerings available here.

Today, a number of wellness services have tuned into the island's rugged and sybaritic sides. Having arrived in Victoria, with its British-influence Parliament buildings, hotel high teas, a genteel oceanfront promenade, I booked it straight to HAVN. After rinsing off the magnesium-infused salt, I stopped at its cozy onboard cafe, which invites lingering in a robe and sipping a coffee or turmeric-based wellness elixir. I disembarked feeling purified and ready to keep exploring.

articles.title: At Costa Rican Wellness Resort, Learning About My 'Human Design'
articles.summary: On the brink of a new chapter in her life, writer Jessica Sulima travels to Costa Rica in hopes of quieting her mind and looking inwards.
body: I’m not usually looking for self-actualization through my travels, but the truth is, I found myself at a time in my life where a wellness retreat in Costa Rica sounded like a really good idea. I was dealing with impending loss, a recent breakup, and an overarching anxiety about getting older. Some might call what I was going through a quarter-life crisis; others, a Saturn return. Surely, I thought, whatever was clouding my mind about turning 30 would clear with the vibrations rippling through The Vessyl’s “Frequency Dome.”
Clouds disperse around the peak of the Arenal Volcano, as seen from the swimming pool of The Vessyl.

I then met a facilitator named Ashley Marie, who would guide me through the Bio-Well scan in the Dome’s lobby. Developed by Russian physicist Konstantin Korotov, Bio-Well is a little cube of a scanner that uses GDV-style imaging (Gas Discharge Visualization) to reflect patterns in stress, balance, energy distribution, and overall regulation—essentially a snapshot of your current energetic state—all taken from your fingerprints alone.
“You guys aren’t gonna clone me, are you?” I asked Wittman, half-jokingly.

articles.title: 7 Fall Decor Trends Worth the Investment, According to Interior Designers
articles.summary: As temperatures continue to drop, transform your space by shopping our favorite fall home decor essentials—here, interior designers share the trends to know.
body: As leaves turn russet and we retrieve our rollneck sweaters and leather boots from the depths of our closets, our interiors deserve a little refresh, too. (What season is better for nesting?) Any designer will tell you that the change needn’t be drastic; something as simple as upgrading your bed linens or introducing a new lamp can make all the difference.

Perhaps now is the time to invest in that piece of furniture you’ve had your eye on, or finally pull together a room that doesn’t quite feel finished with the help of an accent rug. Whatever you’re after, we spoke to 10 interior designers to discover the key fall home decor trends worth buying into this season.

You might assume that fall calls for a color palette of soft browns, reds, oranges, and yellows–but this year, it’s all about the richness of jewel tones and using certain shades with intensity. Take Sophie Rowell, founder of Côte de Folk, who, in one project, recently enveloped walls and floors in a deep olive green, adding a sense of tactility by forgoing hard flooring and rugs in favor of wall-to-wall carpet.

articles.title: 15 Retinol-Rich Foods to Stimulate Collagen and Your Immune System
articles.summary: A doctor weighs in on everything you need to know about the trendy “retinol” diet.
body: Anybody who is serious about anti-aging is using retinol in their beauty routine. The ingredient, which is a derivative of vitamin A, is considered the gold-star anti-aging ingredient when it comes to skin health. Vitamin A—whether it’s in the form of retinol or one of the other retinoids, like retinoic acid or retinyl palmitate—has been clinically proven to smooth lines, clear acne, and reverse sun damage because it supports cellular turnover.

But vitamin A doesn’t just come in a tube. There are plenty of foods that are rich in vitamin A, which is almost totally bioavailable and benefits more than just your skin. Eating a diet rich in vitamin A helps to support healthy immune and reproductive systems; when you’re applying it topically, it’s solely focused on dermal cellular turnover.

“Diet plays a significant role in our skin’s health and appearance,” says Manhattan-based board-certified dermatologist Dendy Engelman, MD, FAAD. “There are studies to support that increased vitamin intake helps skin in both the aging space and acne.”
Here’s how you can take advantage of vitamin A in your diet to improve your skin, immune system, and more.
